Let \(d=\gcd(2m,3n)\).

Since \(m=24n+51\), we have
\[
2m=48n+102.
\]
Thus
\[
d=\gcd(48n+102,\,3n).
\]
Because \(d\mid 3n\), it also divides \(16(3n)=48n\). Therefore
\[
d\mid (48n+102)-48n=102.
\]
So \(d\le 102\).

Now check whether \(d=102\) is possible. We need \(102\mid 3n\), which happens if \(34\mid n\). Choose \(n=34\). Then
\[
m=24(34)+51=867.
\]
Now
\[
2m=1734=102\cdot 17,\qquad 3n=102.
\]
So
\[
\gcd(2m,3n)=\gcd(1734,102)=102.
\]

Therefore, the largest possible value is
\[
\boxed{102}
\]

The answer is 102.
